subject: Television & Streaming
title: The Rise of the Unreliable Narrator
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Rise of the Unreliable Narrator.

hook.text: In Mr. Robot, the protagonist has dissociative identity disorder. Everything he tells the audience might be wrong.

buildup.text: Unreliable narrators existed in literature for centuries but arrived late to television.

discovery.text: Shows like Westworld and The Affair used unreliable perspectives to make viewers question every scene.

twist.text: The technique requires immense trust between show and audience.

climax.text: Unreliable narration transformed television from a medium that shows you truth to one that questions what truth means.

punchline.text: The most honest shows are the ones that admit they might be lying.

quiz.question: What risk does using an unreliable narrator create in television?
options: If viewers feel cheated rather than surprised by the deception, the entire show can lose audience trust
